 Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Isaiah Stewart will start Sunday’s game against the Kings. 
 While Coward returns after a one-game absence and pushes GG Jackson to the bench, the Grizzlies will not play Zach Edey due to injury management. As a result, Stewart will start at center in his second official game for the franchise. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  NBA Lineups

 Cedric Coward (wrist) is available for Sunday’s game against the Kings. 
 Coward is back after sitting out Friday’s win over the Warriors. With his return, GG Jackson will head to the bench after making a spot start the last time out. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward (wrist) is questionable to play against the Kings on Sunday. 
 Coward missed Friday’s game against Golden State, which allowed GG Jackson to start in his place. Coward should start if he’s back, but if not, Jackson may start again, though he only played 15 minutes on Friday, while Jerami Grant played 26 minutes. 
 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Zach Edey (ankle) has been ruled out against the Kings on Sunday. 
 Edey will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back, which means he should be back to take on the Jazz on Monday. Expect Isaiah Stewart to start in his place, with Quinten Post filling out the backup minutes. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart notched four points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds and one steal in Friday’s win over the Warriors. 
 Stewart made his official Grizzlies debut on Friday, playing most of his minutes when starting center Zach Edey (8/10/3/1/2) was not on the floor. Unfortunately, Beef Stew picked up four fouls in the first half, including three in the first quarter, which limited him to 16 minutes. It remains to be seen what his role will look like once the ankle is no longer a concern, but Stewart isn’t someone worth rostering in most redraft leagues just yet. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is available for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Stewart has been cleared to make his Grizzlies debut after spraining his ankle during the preseason. He’ll provide frontcourt depth off the bench, likely resulting in fewer minutes for Quinten Post. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward (wrist) is out for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Initially doubtful with a sprained left wrist, Coward is officially out for Friday’s game. GG Jackson replaces him in the starting lineup and is worth streaming in deep leagues. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Stewart, injured during the preseason, did not play in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz. Quinten Post logged 19 minutes off the bench as the backup center, and he’ll likely keep that role if Beef Stew can’t play on Friday. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward (wrist) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Coward, who played 28 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz, is dealing with a sprained left wrist. With the doubtful tag, he’s more likely to miss Friday. If Coward sits, reserves like Scotty Pippen Jr. and Jerami Grant would get more offensive opportunities. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward had 7 points (3-of-6 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists, a block, and a three. 
 It wasn’t the best outing for Coward who had five fouls in this game. He was being drafted in the 80’s and through the 90’s in redraft leagues. Obviously, you would want more at that price point, but it didn’t happen tonight. He’ll have his next opportunity against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Stewart was initially doubtful for Wednesday’s season opener, so the downgrade in status is not a surprise. Quinten Post should slot in as the backup center behind starter Zach Edey.

 Darius Garland tallied 16 points (7-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, 11 assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder.
 After totaling 10 assists in the Clippers’ first two games of the season, Garland recorded 11 helpers against the Thunder. That said, turnovers remain an issue, as he racked up five in the 108-101 defeat. Over three games, Garland has recorded 21 assists and 17 turnovers. So far, he’s been more valuable in eight-cat formats or to nine-cat managers willing to punt turnovers. The Clippers play three games in Week 2, starting with the Lakers on Wednesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Isaiah Hartenstein recorded 12 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, one assist and one steal in Sunday’s win over the Clippers.
 After recording two underwhelming stat lines in Oklahoma City’s first two games of the season, Hartenstein posted a double-double on Sunday. His play helped offset Chet Holmgren’s quiet night at the office (10 points, four rebounds, one steal, one block and two three-pointers), helping push Oklahoma City’s record to 3-0. Hartenstein also played 27 minutes, an encouraging number given his limited minutes last season. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ajay Mitchell accounted for 18 points (8-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Clippers.
 The Thunder lost Cason Wallace (shoulder) in the first quarter on Sunday. While Mitchell wasn’t the choice to start the third quarter, his role will expand if Wallace misses time. Jared McCain (three points, one rebound, one steal, and one three-pointer) replaced Wallace, and he can provide points and three-pointers in that role. However, Mitchell is the better option for fantasy managers left choosing between the two on the waiver wire. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Karl-Anthony Towns notched 22 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), 14 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in Sunday’s loss to the Magic.
 While Towns has recorded a double-double in each of his first three games this season, that production has not kept the Knicks from going 0-3. Against the Magic, KAT recorded a stat line that only lacked a three-pointer, as he missed all four of his attempts. The Knicks play three games in Week 2, starting Tuesday against the Pistons. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 ORL 
 Forward

 Player Stats

 Franz Wagner tallied 23 points (9-of-23 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds and nine assists in Sunday’s win over the Knicks.
 Wagner had a rough first three quarters on Sunday, scoring two points on 1-of-10 shooting. Something changed in the fourth, as he shot 8-of-13 from the field and 5-of-5 from the foul line. Wagner scored 21 of Orlando’s 40 fourth-quarter points, with the Magic delivering Sean Sweeney his first win as an NBA head coach. Orlando plays three games in Week 2, starting with the Raptors on Wednesday. With Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs injured, Wagner will carry even more of the offensive workload. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Scottie Barnes failed to score in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves, finishing with three rebounds, three assists, four steals and one blocked shot.
 With Kawhi Leonard (knee) unavailable, the Timberwolves could focus more of their defensive attention on Barnes. Unfortunately for the Raptors and fantasy managers who are rostering him, Barnes couldn’t buy a basket. He shot 0-of-12 from the field and did not attempt a free throw. Given Barnes’ track record, managers should expect to see him bounce back from Sunday’s performance. But it was a rough way to end Week 1. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander amassed 34 points (13-of-26 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Clippers.
 On a night when he saw three teammates leave the game with injuries, Gilgeous-Alexander carried the Thunder in the third quarter. The reigning MVP scored 16 of his 34 points in the period, shooting 7-of-11 from the field. SGA went cold in the fourth, but his teammates provided enough help to keep Oklahoma City undefeated. The Thunder play three games in Week 2, starting with the Suns on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Suggs (knee) was helped back to the Magic locker room during the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Suggs was driving to the basket for an uncontested layup when his right knee hyperextended. The Magic guard remained down on the court for a few minutes before being helped back to the locker room. Suggs could put some weight on his right leg, but the injury could keep him out for a while. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Williams exited late in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game against the Clippers after suffering a serious left leg injury. 
 Williams suffered a serious left leg injury late in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game, with team doctors applying an air cast before taking him off the court on a stretcher. He’ll miss an unknown amount of time, but the Thunder forward is likely looking at a lengthy absence. Jared McCain replaced Williams in the Thunder lineup. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ivica Zubac (ankle) unlikely to suit up Monday vs. Bucks.
 The x-ray came back negative on his left ankle, but did leave the arena on crutches due to a swollen ankle. Although the center will most likely be sidelined on Monday vs. the Bucks, Zubac has seemed to avoid any long term injury for now. It’s something for fantasy managers to watch over the next few days.
